subject: Acme rollout — SLA & premium support options for production go-live
messages:
From: Jamie Park <jamie@acme-corp.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: Kelly Park <kelly@acme-corp.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Inquiry: SLA + premium support bundles for Acme production rollout

Hi Sergio,

We're finalizing our production cutover plan for August and need to lock the support package and SLA for our Redwood-powered inference layer. High level: Acme expects a global storefront with low tail latency during Black Friday-like traffic spikes.

Questions we need answered before procurement:
- Uptime options you can commit to (99.5 / 99.9 / 99.99) and the unit economics for each.
- Response windows for P1/P2/P3 incidents and on-call escalation coverage (hours, SLA credits).
- What adds operationally between Standard vs Priority vs Enterprise (how many engineers, paging roster, warm standby replicas?).
- Typical contract/term and any discounts for annual/3-year commits.

We have an internal budget range but flexibility for an annual commit. Can you send a short matrix (uptime vs price vs credits) and call out any constraints that require multi-region Dedicated or warm standby?

Appreciate a reply with options — Kelly is our platform PM and will own the internal acceptance criteria.

Thanks,
Jamie Park
Head of Platform Ops, Acme Cloud
jamie@acme-corp.com

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Park <jamie@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Kelly Park <kelly@acme-corp.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inquiry: SLA + premium support bundles for Acme production rollout

Jamie — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching a concise matrix and a draft SLA for your legal review (attachments: uptime-tiers-v3.xlsx, redwood-sla-draft-20270620.pdf). High-level summary below: 

Packages (summary):
- Standard: 99.5% uptime, P1 response 4 business-hours, 9x5 email + phone escalation, SLA credits = 5% monthly service credit band. Best for non-critical workloads.
- Priority: 99.9% uptime, P1 response 60 minutes during business hours, 24x7/4hr paging for P1, 24x7/8hr for P2, SLA credits = 10% slab. Includes faster triage and dedicated queue.
- Enterprise: 99.99% uptime (multi-region, Dedicated pools + warm standby), P1 immediate paging with dedicated on-call rotation, 24x7/2hr for P1, 24x7/6hr for P2, SLA credits up to 25% for extended outages. Comes with runbook assist and quarterly ops reviews.

Notes on economics and constraints:
- 99.99 requires multi-region Dedicated + warm standby and a higher committed capacity; expect ~2.2x unit cost vs Priority (see spreadsheet tab "cost-assumptions").
- We can offer a one-time 10% annual-commit introductory discount on the first-year invoice for Standard/Priority. Enterprise discounts are handled case-by-case.
- Escalation coverage (Enterprise) includes a named on-call engineer and 2-hour follow-the-sun escalation ladder; additional dedicated engineers are add-ons.

Next steps:
1) Confirm target uptime and whether you want multi-region Dedicated.
2) If you want an introductory discount, indicate annual vs multi-year commit.
3) We can run a short SLO/traffic profile with Karthik's team to validate capacity assumptions.

Cc'ing Rachel/Karthik to coordinate pricing and operational feasibility.

— Sergio Alvarez
Sr. Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Attachments: uptime-tiers-v3.xlsx, redwood-sla-draft-20270620.pdf

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Park <jamie@acme-corp.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inquiry: SLA + premium support bundles for Acme production rollout

Jamie — quick clarifying questions from the commercial side: 
- Do you expect read/write traffic to be global (EU/APAC) at go-live, or primarily NA with future regions? This affects whether multi-region Dedicated is required immediately.
- What contract term are you evaluating (12 / 36 months)? We typically price discounts differently for 3-year commitments.
- Any internal procurement constraints (PO, SOC 2 evidence, indemnity) we should loop legal on now? Laura — please flag anything contract-side to prep.

If you confirm target uptime = 99.9, I can produce a clean pricing quote + MLP (Mutual Action Plan) for next-week signatures.

Thanks,
Rachel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Jamie Park <jamie@acme-corp.com>, Kelly Park <kelly@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 12:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inquiry: SLA + premium support bundles for Acme production rollout

Quick technical read:
- If Acme needs 99.9 and traffic is NA-first, Priority (single-region Dedicated with routing-based fallback) is usually sufficient. 99.99 requires a warm-standby region with active/passive failover and consistent KV cache warmup; that adds both infra and runbook overhead.
- Operationally the jump from 99.9 -> 99.99: expect additional 1.5-2 FTE-equivalent on-call coverage (distributed), automated health-checks + faster failover playbooks, regular DR drills.
- Escalation matrix (recommended for Enterprise): Page -> On-call engineer (15m), Escalate to SWAT (2hr), Exec notify (4hr). For Priority, we recommend Page -> Ops triage (60m) -> Engineering follow-up (4hr).

I'll run a quick capacity delta once Jamie confirms traffic footprint (QPS distribution by region + peak window).

— Karthik
Director, Serving Runtime Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Jamie Park <jamie@acme-corp.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Kelly Park <kelly@acme-corp.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 15:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inquiry: SLA + premium support bundles for Acme production rollout

Thanks for the thorough summary. A few points from Acme: 
- Go-live must support NA + EU in phase 1; APAC is phase 2. So we likely need multi-region considerations for higher availability.
- Target we're comfortable committing to operationally: 99.9 for first year, with clear runway to 99.99 by Q4.
- Budget posture: if Redwood will agree to a 20% discount on the Enterprise feature-set (we don't need all add-ons immediately — e.g., just 24x7 paging + named on-call + quarterly reviews) in exchange for a 24-month annualized commitment, we can sign a PO quickly.
- We do require SOC 2 Type II evidence and standard indemnity language; happy to share PO template.

If you can provide a redlined quote and a mutual action plan this week, we will route the PO for signatures.

Jamie
Head of Platform Ops, Acme Cloud

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Park <jamie@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 20:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inquiry: SLA + premium support bundles for Acme production rollout

Jamie — appreciated. I'm escalating the 20% Enterprise concession and 24-month ask to our commercial leadership; Laura will handle contract redlines (SOC 2 and indemnity). Two items I can commit to immediately:
1) We'll deliver a Mutual Action Plan and a redlined quote by EOD Wednesday (includes a scoped Enterprise bundle that strips optional add-ons you flagged).
2) I'll open a HubSpot deal (linked) and add a short DocuSign flow for the PO/Initial SOW once pricing is approved.

Laura — if we can pre-approve a limited one-time concession (20% off Enterprise SKU conditional on the 24-month commit and a 30% prepayment on invoice 1), we can expedite signature this week.

Jamie/Kelly — expect the MAP + pricing PDF and a Call invite for Wednesday AM for a brief alignment.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Sr. Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
